# std::linalg::spectral

<!-- Generated by scripts/check_spec.py from docs/spec/std-linalg-spectral.toml. Edit that file and run `python3 scripts/check_spec.py --write`. -->

The properties of the exact spectral profile of polynomial matrix fields, from ADR 0001 §12. Let A be the ring of the polynomials with exact rational coefficients in the coordinates of a smooth affine object X. A free module V on X is Aⁿ with a named basis, with n at most 4, and an endomorphism field H of V is an n × n matrix over A. The spectral pair of H has the characteristic polynomial χ = det(tI − H) in A[t], with a named fiber coordinate t, and the module V on which t acts as H. A branch is a finite chart D(g) of the spectrum, certified by a witness W with W·χ′ ≡ gᵉ modulo χ, on which every eigenvalue is simple. The module declares the families `FreeModule<X>`, `Endomorphism<X>`, `Spectrum<X>` and `Branch<X>`. The application declares each module, field, spectrum and branch, the invariants `trace_power` and `char_coefficient`, and the observations `annihilates`, `action_entry`, `on_branch`, `branch_differential` and `branch_projector`. The failure value ⊥ lies over no point.

[Specifications](../specifications.md) defines the [claim statuses](../specifications.md#claim-statuses) and the checks. This chapter is generated from [`docs/spec/std-linalg-spectral.toml`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/docs/spec/std-linalg-spectral.toml).

<a id="spectral.static-identity"></a>

## Objects and spectra are static

- Property: `spectral.static-identity`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral::Spectrum`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-2)

A field acts on a free module of its own object, a spectrum is the spectrum of a field of its own object, and a branch is a chart of a spectrum of its own object; any other declaration is an error (`E_SPECTRAL`). An observation names its spectrum or its branch in its binding. It accepts a point only of the object of that spectrum or branch, and a branch observation accepts an eigenvalue only on its declared line. Any other operand is an error (`E_ENDPOINT`).

- Example: On the plane, let H = rows((x, y), (y, −x)) act on V = basis(e1, e2). A field `rows((u, v), (v, −u))` of V on a second plane with the coordinates u and v is an error (`E_SPECTRAL`), although both planes have the dimension 2. An observation of the spectrum of the field 2I on the point, applied to a point of the plane, is an error (`E_ENDPOINT`).
- Run by: `spectral_mismatches_are_rejected_statically` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)

Claims:

- `binding`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.SpectralPrimitives`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SpectralPrimitives.lean): `VastitasOracle.SpectralPrimitives.annihilates_association`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralPrimitives.actionEntry_association`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralPrimitives.onBranch_association`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralPrimitives.branchDifferential_association`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralPrimitives.branchProjector_association`

The kernel's typing of a call reads that association, so the theorems concern checked bindings, and the Rust frontend relates them to source declarations.

<a id="spectral.pair"></a>

## The spectral pair is computed and checked

- Property: `spectral.pair`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral::Spectrum`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-2)

For a spectrum `eigen(H, t)` the kernel computes χ = det(tI − H) and adj(tI − H), and accepts the declaration only when χ equals the cofactor determinant of tI − H, (tI − H)·adj = χ·I, the trace of the adjugate is χ′, χ(H) = 0, adj² − χ′·adj is a multiple of χ, and Jacobi's formula ∂ᵢχ + tr(adj·∂ᵢH) = 0 holds for each coordinate. Every identity modulo χ is checked against a quotient that the kernel computes. No characteristic polynomial, adjugate or quotient comes from the source or the wire.

- Example: For H = rows((x, y), (y, −x)) the kernel computes χ = t² − x² − y² and adj(tI − H) = tI + H. A spectrum record with a field `characteristic`, `adjugate` or `quotient` is an error (`E_PROTOCOL`).
- Run by: `raw_wire_rejects_spectral_certificates_and_forged_maps` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)

Claims:

- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `raw_wire_rejects_spectral_certificates_and_forged_maps` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)

<a id="spectral.module-action"></a>

## The module action tells fields apart

- Property: `spectral.module-action`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral::Spectrum`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-2)

`annihilates(…, spectrum = S, element = f)` at a point p is true exactly when f(H(p)) = 0, and `action_entry(…, spectrum = S, element = f, eᵢ, eⱼ)` is the entry (eᵢ, eⱼ) of f(H(p)), for f in A[t]. The spectrum is the characteristic scheme of H, never its reduced spectrum or the locus of an annihilator: two fields with the same χ, the same trace powers and the same coefficients can differ in their module action.

- Example: On the point, 2I and J = [[2, 1], [0, 2]] both have χ = (t − 2)², the trace powers 4 and 8 and the same coefficients. t − 2 annihilates 2I and not J, and the entry (f1, f2) of J − 2I is 1, that of 2I − 2I is 0. (t − 2)² annihilates both (Cayley–Hamilton). The fields 0 and N = [[0, 1], [0, 0]] differ in the same way.
- Run by: `the_example_checks_builds_and_prints_42_in_place` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)

<a id="spectral.invariants"></a>

## Invariants are smooth maps

- Property: `spectral.invariants`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral::Endomorphism`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-2)

`trace_power(H, k)`, for 1 ≤ k ≤ 8, is the smooth map tr(Hᵏ) from the object of H to a line, and `char_coefficient(S, i)` is the coefficient of tⁱ in χ. Each is an ordinary smooth map: its differential, its gradient under a metric and its compiled reverse pass are those of `std::differential`, and it has no reverse rule of its own. The kernel computes the map from the declaration; a map on the wire is an error (`E_PROTOCOL`).

- Example: For H = rows((x, y), (y, −x)), `trace_power(H, 2)` is the map 2x² + 2y², equal to the map `pullback(t -> 2*x^2 + 2*y^2)`. Its gradient on the dimensionless Euclidean chart is (4x, 4y): (4, 8) at (1, 2) and (0, 0) at the origin. tr(H) is 0, whose differential is the zero covector over the point and not ⊥, and the coefficient of t⁰ is −x² − y², whose gradient is −1/2 that of tr(H²).
- Run by: `the_example_checks_builds_and_prints_42_in_place` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)

<a id="spectral.branch-chart"></a>

## A branch is a certified finite chart

- Property: `spectral.branch-chart`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral::Branch`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Negative tests](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#negative-tests-2)

`simple(S, localize = g, witness = W, exponent = e)` is accepted only when g is a nonzero polynomial in the coordinates of the object, without the fiber coordinate, W has degree below n in t, e ≤ 8, and W·χ′ − gᵉ is a multiple of χ, which the kernel checks against a quotient that it computes. Any other chart is an error (`E_SPECTRAL`). On D(g) every eigenvalue of H(p) is simple.

- Example: For χ = t² − x² − y², the witness t/2 certifies D(x² + y²): (t/2)·2t = t² is x² + y² modulo χ. The same witness with g = 1 is an error, because the eigenvalues meet at the origin, and so is the witness (1/2 + 10⁻²⁰)t. The Jordan block [[2, 1], [0, 2]] has no chart, because χ′ = 2(t − 2) is nilpotent modulo χ = (t − 2)².
- Run by: `rejected_stage5_packages_print_their_diagnostics` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)

<a id="spectral.branch-observations"></a>

## Branch points, differentials and eigenprojectors

- Property: `spectral.branch-observations`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral::Branch`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Laws](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#laws-2)

Let p be a point and t a rational on the line. `on_branch` is true exactly when g(p) ≠ 0 and χ(p, t) = 0. At such a branch point, `branch_differential` is the covector −Σᵢ (∂ᵢχ / χ′)(p, t) dxᵢ, and `branch_projector` with eᵢ and eⱼ is the entry (eᵢ, eⱼ) of adj(tI − H(p)) / χ′(p, t). Off the chart the differential is ⊥ and an entry reads (0, 0). No observation computes, orders or chooses an eigenvalue.

- Example: At p = (3, 4) the eigenvalues 5 and −5 are on the branch of D(x² + y²), and 4 is not; the origin is off the chart, although χ(0, 0) = 0 at t = 0. The differentials are (3/5, 4/5) and (−3/5, −4/5), unit covectors under the Euclidean metric, and the eigenprojectors are (1/5)[[4, 2], [2, 1]] and (1/5)[[1, −2], [−2, 4]].
- Run by: `the_example_checks_builds_and_prints_42_in_place` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)

<a id="spectral.limits"></a>

## The finite profile

- Property: `spectral.limits`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral::FreeModule`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Execution and evidence profile](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#execution-and-evidence-profile-2)

A free module has at most 4 basis vectors (`spectralRank`), and a trace power and the exponent of a branch are at most 8 (`spectralPower`). Every polynomial that the kernel reads or computes for a field, a spectral pair, a trace power or a witness check is within the term limit, and its computation within the work budget, of the exact algebra. Beyond a limit the declaration is an error (`E_LIMIT`), reported before any identity is compared.

- Example: A free module with the basis e1, …, e5 is an error (`E_LIMIT`), and so is `trace_power(H, 9)`. A symmetric 4 × 4 field whose entries are the 455-term polynomial (1 + x0 + … + x11)³ stops on the work budget while its spectral pair is computed.
- Run by: `the_rank_is_bounded_at_the_free_module` in [`tests/spectral_limits.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_limits.rs)

Claims:

- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `the_rank_is_bounded_at_the_free_module` in [`tests/spectral_limits.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_limits.rs)
    - `powers_and_exponents_are_bounded` in [`tests/spectral_limits.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_limits.rs)
